sectionsUsed: 3.1 Objects, values and types: every object has an identity, a type and a value; the is operator compares identity; objects whose value can change are mutable; numbers, strings and tuples are immutable, dictionaries and lists are mutable
Why are default values shared between objects?: default values are created exactly once, when the function is defined; use None and create the list inside
Why did changing list y also change list x?: variables are names that refer to objects; y = x does not copy
How do I copy an object in Python?: copy.copy() and copy.deepcopy(); sequences can be copied by slicing
4.9.1 Default Argument Values: important warning, the default value is evaluated only once, which matters for a mutable object such as a list; use None
4.8 Defining Functions: arguments are passed using call by value, where the value is always an object reference
Assignment statements do not copy objects; a shallow copy inserts references to the objects found in the original; a deep copy inserts copies; dict.copy() and slicing make shallow copies
